title: Native constructibility of ordinary integral finite local models
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite. Fix an embedding $i:E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a normalized coefficient presentation $C$ with its native section functor $S$, as in [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data]. Let $N$ be an ordinary module sheaf over the detailed completed integral coefficient. Restrict N along the fixed projection-normalized completed coefficient comparison of [def-sfb-integral-completed-coefficient-transport]. Suppose this restriction has stratified finitely presented integral constant local models in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-models]: some finite locally closed stratification admits pro-etale covering sieves on which it is the completed constant realization of a finitely presented valuation-ring module. If $F$ is a native adic sheaf and $S(F)\simeq\operatorname{pbcExtend}(C.\mathrm{integralMap})(N)$, then F is native adic constructible. Only ordinary sheaves occur; there is no hypothesis or conclusion about derived objects.

proof.text: The given coefficient restriction is along an isomorphism. On the stratification and covering sieves in hN, its inverse identifies N with the same finite integral presentations over the detailed coefficient. The continuous integral module encoding carries these models to locally finitely presented internal modules on these strata.

Use the normalizations in C to identify the coefficient action with integral inclusion, localization and the embedding i. The internal-section scalar-adjunction comparison identifies ordinary extension with internal extension, by b tensor m mapping to the identical balanced tensor. Such extension commutes with actual-ring inverse image and with slice restriction, by uniqueness of the scalar-extension left adjoint. It preserves finite presentations and the same local covering families, so the resulting internal algebraic-closure module is constructible on the original finite stratification.

The native encoding is fully faithful and reflects native constructibility. Apply its constructibility equivalence to the internal local models, and use the displayed ordinary isomorphism to transfer the result to F. Concretely, each scalar finite presentation becomes a finite-dimensional vector space after localization and then a finite free native module after extension along i. Pure torsion gives rank zero; an empty stratum or empty scheme is allowed.
